 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227
Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To:
 1. Issue A Writ In The Nature Of Mandamus Directing
The Land Acquisition Officer To Pass General Award Under
Section 23 Of The Right To Fair Compensation And
Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And
Resettlement Act, 2013, In Respect Of The Petitioner'S
Lands.

2. ISSUE A WRIT IN THE NATURE OF MANDAMUS DIRECTING THE RESPONDENT NO.6 TO CONSIDER THE REPRESENTATIONS OF THE PETITIONERS DATED 19.03.2024 RECEIVED ON 01.04.2024 PRODUCED AT ANNEXURES-C, C1 TO C41 AND TO PASS GENERAL AWARD IN RESPECT OF THE PETITIONER'S LANDS CONCERN AND ETC.

- 11 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914  WP No. 102463 of 2024  THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B'
GROUP THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent/state and the learned counsel Sri. Chetan Munnoli for respondent No.4.
2.

The petitioners filed this petition seeking for a writ of mandamus direction to the Land Acquisition Officer to pass a general award under Section 23 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013') in respect of petitioners' lands and consequently to consider their representations dated 19.03.2024 and 01.04.2024 to respondent No.6.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is a case of petitioners that they are the owners of the respective lands mentioned in the chart filed along with the writ petition.
The said lands of the petitioners were acquired under the Upper Krishna project by the respondents.
All the petitioners are aggrieved by a common grievance in respect of common cause of action, which is the non inaction of the respondents in passing final award.
Due to the submergence of the lands in view of the height of Almatti Dam having been raised, the lands of the petitioners got submerged.

Therefore, a preliminary notification under Section 11(1) of Shri. Malappa S/O Annappa Kurani Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162118957/

sentences.text: the Act, 2013 was issued on 05.03.2022, which came to be published on the 28.03.2022.
Subsequently, a declaration was issued under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 on 14.01.2022, and the same came to be published on 28.12.2022.
4. The Land Acquisition Officer/respondent No.6
issued a notice under Sections 21(1) and (2) of the Act, 2013 for measurement and possession of the land.
This being the state of affairs in view of coming into force of the 2013 Act, where there is no provision for passing of consent award.

But however, the state of Karnataka has included an amendment to Section 23 as 23(a) inserted vide Karnataka Act of 2016 of 2019 which empowers the authority to pass an award without holding any enquiry under Section 23, thereby based on which the Deputy Commissioner has the authority to pass an award without conducting an inquiry under Section 23(a) on consent award.

Accordingly,
notification was issued under Rule 30(A)(1)(2).

The petitioners initially agreed for the offer made - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914 by the Land Acquisition Officer to pass the consent award under Section 23(a), despite which the respondents did not pass the consent award and later the petitioners realized that the consent award which the petitioners had agreed was not in their interest as it was lesser than the prevailing market price available as on the said date.

Hence, the petitioners withdraw the consent and requested the respondents to pass a general award in respect of their lands and a representation was made on 19.03.2024, which was received on 01.04.2024 by the respondents.
5.
This being the state of affairs, though the land of the petitioners has been submerged and acquired, the respondents have failed to pass the award.

Hence, due to the inaction of the respondents, the petitioners are before this Court seeking a direction for respondent No.6 to pass the award and disburse the compensation to the petitioners.
6.

Learned counsel for respondent No.4 vehemently contends that there is no provision for the petitioners to withdraw the consent after having given consent for passing of the award and subsequently withdrawing the consent is not - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914 permissible.
Hence, he contends that the writ petition is not maintainable and the same requires to be dismissed.
7. So also learned AGA supports the arguments canvassed by respondent No.4 with regard to the petitioners not having the liberty to withdraw the consent.
Once consent is given for passing the consent award, he also seeks for dismissal of the petition.

8. It is not in dispute that the lands of the petitioners were submerged and a notification came to be issued by the respondents for acquisition of the lands and also a final notification is issued on 14.12.2022 under Section 19 of the Act, 2013, but the award is not passed yet.
It is relevant to note that, as per Section 25 of the Act, 2013, the period within which award is to be made is twelve Shri.

12 months from the date of publication of declaration under Section 19 of the Act, 2013 and in case no such award is made within the said period, a further period of twelve months is provided for passing the award by recording proper reasons for the same.

sentences.text: In the present case there is no such extension and neither is the award passed within a period of twelve months as specified under the Act, 2013.
As stated earlier, there is no dispute with regard to the lands of the petitioners having been submerged and acquired by the respondents by virtue of a final notification also passed on 14.12.2022.
There is nothing that is required further for the respondents to do, except to pass the award and disburse the compensation in favour of the petitioners.
10. Under the circumstances, the respondents cannot keep quiet and stay silent.
The state government, being the "Parens patriae" and the guardian of the citizens, cannot act in a manner which is contrary to law and against the constitution.

Petitioners as a matter of right are entitled to enjoy their property as a constitutional right as per Article 300A and in case the state wants to acquire, the same shall be done in accordance with law and in the manner known to law for itself or for the beneficiary.

11. In the present case the same having not been done within a reasonable time and the further extended time provided under the act duty is cast upon the state to immediately pass the award and disburse the compensation to the petitioners in accordance with law.

Therefore, I pass the following:
- 16 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914  ORDER  i) The petition is allowed.
 ii) The writ of mandamus is issued to respondent Nos.5 and 6 to pass the general award with respect to the lands of the petitioners mentioned herein in this petition in accordance with law and disburse the same immediately iii) The award shall be passed within an outer limit of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners filed this petition seeking for a writ of mandamus direction to the Land Acquisition Officer to pass a general award under Section 23 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013') in respect of petitioners' lands and consequently to consider their representations dated 19.03.2024 and 01.04.2024 to respondent No.6.
Subsequently, a declaration was issued under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 on 14.01.2022, and the same came to be published on 28.12.2022.
issued a notice under Sections 21(1) and (2) of the Act, 2013 for measurement and possession of the land.
The petitioners initially agreed for the offer made - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914 by the Land Acquisition Officer to pass the consent award under Section 23(a), despite which the respondents did not pass the consent award and later the petitioners realized that the consent award which the petitioners had agreed was not in their interest as it was lesser than the prevailing market price available as on the said date.
Hence, the petitioners withdraw the consent and requested the respondents to pass a general award in respect of their lands and a representation was made on 19.03.2024, which was received on 01.04.2024 by the respondents.
5.
Hence, due to the inaction of the respondents, the petitioners are before this Court seeking a direction for respondent No.6 to pass the award and disburse the compensation to the petitioners.
6.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel for respondent No.4 vehemently contends that there is no provision for the petitioners to withdraw the consent after having given consent for passing of the award and subsequently withdrawing the consent is not - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914 permissible.
Hence, he contends that the writ petition is not maintainable and the same requires to be dismissed.
7. So also learned AGA supports the arguments canvassed by respondent No.4 with regard to the petitioners not having the liberty to withdraw the consent.
Once consent is given for passing the consent award, he also seeks for dismissal of the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the present case there is no such extension and neither is the award passed within a period of twelve months as specified under the Act, 2013.
There is nothing that is required further for the respondents to do, except to pass the award and disburse the compensation in favour of the petitioners.
The state government, being the "Parens patriae" and the guardian of the citizens, cannot act in a manner which is contrary to law and against the constitution.
opennyai_summary.decision:
10. Under the circumstances, the respondents cannot keep quiet and stay silent.
Petitioners as a matter of right are entitled to enjoy their property as a constitutional right as per Article 300A and in case the state wants to acquire, the same shall be done in accordance with law and in the manner known to law for itself or for the beneficiary.
11. In the present case the same having not been done within a reasonable time and the further extended time provided under the act duty is cast upon the state to immediately pass the award and disburse the compensation to the petitioners in accordance with law.
Therefore, I pass the following:
- 16 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7914  ORDER  i) The petition is allowed.
 ii) The writ of mandamus is issued to respondent Nos.5 and 6 to pass the general award with respect to the lands of the petitioners mentioned herein in this petition in accordance with law and disburse the same immediately iii) The award shall be passed within an outer limit of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
